name: ArtScience Museum
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; owner Marina Bay Sands posts annual reports and parent Las Vegas Sands files 10-Ks with the SEC.

name: Artspace Aotearoa
funding: Creative New Zealand (NZ$637k a year for 2027 to 2029) and Auckland Council lead; strategic partners are Chartwell Trust, Foundation North, Goethe-Institut and Wesfarmers.
watch: Wesfarmers is mostly Bunnings and Kmart; its chemicals, energy and fertilisers division, which holds gas retailer Kleenheat, is about 5 percent of group revenue.

name: Asian Art Museum
funding: Foundation expenses $39.4M (FY2025); City of San Francisco, Chong-Moon Lee (tech) gift, trustees.
watch: Current corporate partners include Bloomberg Philanthropies (campaign list), PG&E (gas utility) and COSCO Shipping.
why_flagged: Current corporate partners include Bloomberg Philanthropies (campaign list), PG&E (gas utility) and COSCO Shipping.

name: Aspen Art Museum
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025, it names National Council members undated and lists its trustees, but posts no annual reports.

name: Astrup Fearnley Museet
funding: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality, the Thomas Fearnley, Heddy and Nils Astrup and Hans Rasmus Astrup foundations, and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB; sponsors EGD Holding and The Thief.
watch: Private museum on Oslo's waterfront, founded by shipping magnate Hans Rasmus Astrup. Its endowment comes from global shipping and offshore maritime logistics; it is subject to Norwegian foundation oversight.
why_flagged: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality, the Thomas Fearnley, Heddy and Nils Astrup and Hans Rasmus Astrup foundations, and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB; sponsors EGD Holding and The Thief.
records_note: The museum posts no annual report, but its accounts are in Norway's register, its board is named and funders and sponsors are listed undated.

name: Bait Al Zubair
watch: Fossil fuel money is its founding and current funding. The Zubair Corporation founded the museum (opened by the family). It created Zubair Oil & Gas in the early 1990s, and its unit ARA Petroleum explores for and produces hydrocarbons in Oman and Tanzania.

name: BAK, basis voor actuele kunst
funding: Until 2024 the culture ministry (64 percent) and Utrecht (31 percent) paid 97 percent of EUR 1.98M income. Both ended multi-year funding from 2025; 2025 income fell to EUR 538k. Utrecht grants Basecamp EUR 62,500 a year for 2027 to 2028.
watch: Utrecht ended its multi-year subsidy from 2025 despite a positive advisory report, BAK says; the Council for Culture advised ending state funding. Four post-academic institutions wrote in support.

records_note: Its ANBI page posts annual reports 2021 to 2025 with balance sheets, names seven funders in an undated list, and lists the supervisory board.

name: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity

Suncor and Shell Canada were current donors in 2022-23. Excluded fossil-fuel funders on the campaign list (Shell, BP, Chevron) are current or long-standing donors.

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
watch: Politically tinged defunding 2018; 2025 works removed under embassy pressure.
why_flagged: Politically tinged defunding 2018; 2025 works removed under embassy pressure.
records_note: Its site lists the foundation committee and named supporters, but it blocked page fetches, so annual reports and accounts could not be checked.

name: Bangkok Kunsthalle
funding: Her husband Soopakij chairs CP Group, Thailand's largest private company.
watch: artn't activists staged a guerrilla protest inside, in shirts reading 'world class exploitation'. CP Group's CP Foods faced 2014 slavery claims in its prawn-feed chain.
why_flagged: Opened January 2024 by philanthropist Marisa Chearavanont through her Khao Yai Art; no sponsors are named. She is married to Soopakij Chearavanont, chairman of CP Group.
records_note: Its site now redirects to a script-built page that showed only headings, so nothing was checked.

name: Bard College
watch: Leon Botstein, Bard's president from 1975 to 2026, pursued Epstein as a donor from 2012 to 2019, and Epstein gave to Bard through his foundation Enhanced Education in 2011 and 2012. Epstein attended concerts at Bard's Fisher Center.
why_flagged: Open Society Foundations gave $500M in 2021 to start a $1B endowment campaign, now complete. Epstein's Enhanced Education gave to Bard High School Early College in 2011 and 2012.
records_note: bard.edu has no annual report or financial statements; ProPublica holds Form 990s and audits, a 2018-19 gifts report names donors, and 36 trustees are listed.

name: Bengal Foundation
funding: Private trust founded in 1986, funded entirely by the Bengal Group. Chairman Abul Khair Litu co-founded AB Bank. It runs a fine arts gallery, a music festival and publishing.
watch: In July 2024 the Anti-Corruption Commission endorsed a charge sheet against Litu for acquiring about Tk 903 million in assets beyond his income.
why_flagged: In July 2024 the Anti-Corruption Commission endorsed a charge sheet against Litu for acquiring about Tk 903 million in assets beyond his income.
records_note: Names its Board of Trustees and says the trustees fund it; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published.
